headline: Bank of America has put about 4,000 people, including 1,000 hired contractors, to work fixing software flaws that AI models like Anthropic's Mythos have found.
score_reason: Concrete cost-and-staffing figure from one of the biggest US banks; cost of patching alone not given.
importance_line: Bank staff, customers and other large companies learn what AI-found security holes cost to fix, though the bank gave no separate figure for the patching work.
summary: The Decoder reports, citing CNBC, that Bank of America has hired 1,000 outside contractors to fix software weaknesses found by AI models such as Anthropic's Mythos, working with 3,000 of its own staff since the second quarter, according to chief executive Brian Moynihan. He gave a combined spending figure of a few hundred million dollars for the third quarter for this work and anti-money-laundering requirements, not a separate figure for patching.
notes: Full text read at The Decoder (short). Original CNBC report not read. Headline total of 4,000 is 1,000 contractors plus 3,000 employees.
